blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 3.17
blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 3.17

blocks.text: स्वमात्रानिर्माणमापादयति
blocks.directed: [slowly] स्वमात्रानिर्माणमापादयति

blocks.text: Svamātrānirmāṇam āpādayati.
blocks.directed: Svamātrānirmāṇam āpādayati.

blocks.text: The yogi brings about manifestation according to the measure of their own consciousness.
blocks.directed: The yogi brings about manifestation according to the measure of their own consciousness.

blocks.text: Congratulations, the Universe Is Now Made to Your Measurements.
blocks.directed: Congratulations, the Universe Is Now Made to Your Measurements.

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.directed: [short pause] Right.

blocks.text: We’ve emerged from the Great Lake.
blocks.directed: We’ve emerged from the Great Lake.

blocks.text: Feeling refreshed.
blocks.directed: Feeling refreshed.

blocks.text: Lovely immersion.
blocks.directed: Lovely immersion.

blocks.text: Very peaceful.
blocks.directed: Very peaceful.

blocks.text: And Vasugupta informs us that the realised yogi can now manifest forms according to the power of consciousness.
blocks.directed: And Vasugupta informs us that the realised yogi can now manifest forms according to the power of consciousness.

blocks.text: Naturally.
blocks.directed: Naturally.

blocks.text: Let’s unpack the compound.
blocks.directed: Let’s unpack the compound.

blocks.text: Sva — one’s own.
blocks.directed: Sva — one’s own.

blocks.text: Mātrā — measure, dimension, determining aspect.
blocks.directed: Mātrā — measure, dimension, determining aspect.

blocks.text: Nirmāṇa — production, formation, construction, manifestation.
blocks.directed: Nirmāṇa — production, formation, construction, manifestation.

blocks.text: Āpādayati — brings about, accomplishes, causes to arise.
blocks.directed: Āpādayati — brings about, accomplishes, causes to arise.

blocks.text: The idea is that the yogi manifests according to svamātrā, the measure belonging to their own consciousness.
blocks.directed: The idea is that the yogi manifests according to svamātrā, the measure belonging to their own consciousness.

blocks.text: But Kṣemarāja doesn’t leave mātrā as a vague expression.
blocks.directed: But Kṣemarāja doesn’t leave mātrā as a vague expression.

blocks.text: He gives a fascinating explanation.
blocks.directed: He gives a fascinating explanation.

blocks.text: It is a contracted or condensed aspect of the essence of consciousness.
blocks.directed: It is a contracted or condensed aspect of the essence of consciousness.

blocks.text: Cidrasāśyānatā.
blocks.directed: [slowly] Cidrasāśyānatā.

blocks.text: A kind of solidification of the essence of consciousness.
blocks.directed: A kind of solidification of the essence of consciousness.

blocks.text: Not literal physical solidification, of course.
blocks.directed: Not literal physical solidification, of course.

blocks.text: This is a metaphysical description.
blocks.directed: This is a metaphysical description.

blocks.text: But the imagery is extraordinary.
blocks.directed: But the imagery is extraordinary.

blocks.text: Imagine consciousness as unlimited, self-luminous reality.
blocks.directed: Imagine consciousness as unlimited, self-luminous reality.

blocks.text: And now imagine forms appearing through particular differentiations of that reality.
blocks.directed: And now imagine forms appearing through particular differentiations of that reality.

blocks.text: Objects.
blocks.directed: Objects.

blocks.text: Subjects.
blocks.directed: Subjects.

blocks.text: Bodies.
blocks.directed: Bodies.

blocks.text: Worlds.
blocks.directed: Worlds.

blocks.text: The undivided reality manifests determinate forms.
blocks.directed: The undivided reality manifests determinate forms.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja connects this to the appearance of both vedya and vedaka.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja connects this to the appearance of both vedya and vedaka.

blocks.text: The knowable.
blocks.directed: The knowable.

blocks.text: And the knower.
blocks.directed: And the knower.

blocks.text: Now this is important.
blocks.directed: Now this is important.

blocks.text: We’re not simply saying that consciousness produces an external object which a separate subject subsequently encounters.
blocks.directed: We’re not simply saying that consciousness produces an external object which a separate subject subsequently encounters.

blocks.text: The entire relation between subject and object belongs to manifestation.
blocks.directed: The entire relation between subject and object belongs to manifestation.

blocks.text: The knower and the known are both included in the field of Śakti’s expression.
blocks.directed: The knower and the known are both included in the field of Śakti’s expression.

blocks.text: And here’s where the text becomes especially beautiful.
blocks.directed: And here’s where the text becomes especially beautiful.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja cites the Svacchandatantra to explain that one reality can appear in gross and subtle forms according to its limiting conditions.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja cites the Svacchandatantra to explain that one reality can appear in gross and subtle forms according to its limiting conditions.

blocks.text: Then he turns to the Pratyabhijñā tradition.
blocks.directed: Then he turns to the Pratyabhijñā tradition.

blocks.text: And finally to the relationship between water and ice.
blocks.directed: And finally to the relationship between water and ice.

blocks.text: Now, think about ice.
blocks.directed: Now, think about ice.

blocks.text: Ice has a definite structure.
blocks.directed: Ice has a definite structure.

blocks.text: It can appear as a cube.
blocks.directed: It can appear as a cube.

blocks.text: A sheet.
blocks.directed: A sheet.

blocks.text: A beautifully sculpted swan at an unnecessarily extravagant wedding.
blocks.directed: A beautifully sculpted swan at an unnecessarily extravagant wedding.

blocks.text: And you can describe those forms as distinct objects.
blocks.directed: And you can describe those forms as distinct objects.

blocks.text: But none of them is a substance fundamentally alien to water.
blocks.directed: But none of them is a substance fundamentally alien to water.

blocks.text: The differentiation of form doesn’t establish an independent material reality.
blocks.directed: The differentiation of form doesn’t establish an independent material reality.

blocks.text: That’s the direction of the analogy.
blocks.directed: That’s the direction of the analogy.

blocks.text: Within Trika, the entire manifest universe is understood as the expression of consciousness through its own powers.
blocks.directed: Within Trika, the entire manifest universe is understood as the expression of consciousness through its own powers.

blocks.text: And the realised yogi is said to recognise, and in the traditional account exercise, the creative freedom underlying these manifestations.
blocks.directed: And the realised yogi is said to recognise, and in the traditional account exercise, the creative freedom underlying these manifestations.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja even invokes the Spandakārikā on the yogi who experiences the entire universe as divine play while remaining established in recognition.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja even invokes the Spandakārikā on the yogi who experiences the entire universe as divine play while remaining established in recognition.

blocks.text: And he connects this with jīvanmukti.
blocks.directed: And he connects this with jīvanmukti.

blocks.text: Liberation while living. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: Liberation while living. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: Now, let’s be precise.
blocks.directed: Now, let’s be precise.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja’s commentary really does speak in terms of manifestation according to will.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja’s commentary really does speak in terms of manifestation according to will.

blocks.text: We shouldn’t quietly rewrite his claim into:
blocks.directed: [short pause] We shouldn’t quietly rewrite his claim into:

blocks.text: “You can imagine things creatively.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “You can imagine things creatively.”

blocks.text: That would be a much weaker statement.
blocks.directed: That would be a much weaker statement.

blocks.text: But neither should we mistake the traditional claim for an experimentally established ability to create physical objects by thought.
blocks.directed: But neither should we mistake the traditional claim for an experimentally established ability to create physical objects by thought.

blocks.text: The commentary’s metaphysical point is that the manifesting power of consciousness is not ultimately external to the realised Self.
blocks.directed: The commentary’s metaphysical point is that the manifesting power of consciousness is not ultimately external to the realised Self.

blocks.text: And here’s the wonderful reversal.
blocks.directed: And here’s the wonderful reversal.

blocks.text: In ordinary life, the individual experiences a world that seems to confront them from outside.
blocks.directed: In ordinary life, the individual experiences a world that seems to confront them from outside.

blocks.text: The world is already there.
blocks.directed: The world is already there.

blocks.text: The person is thrown into it.
blocks.directed: The person is thrown into it.

blocks.text: They encounter objects.
blocks.directed: They encounter objects.

blocks.text: They react to circumstances.
blocks.directed: They react to circumstances.

blocks.text: And the entire situation appears governed by powers that are not their own.
blocks.directed: And the entire situation appears governed by powers that are not their own.

blocks.text: But in the supreme recognition described here, the yogi apprehends the world as manifestation of their own universal conscious nature.
blocks.directed: But in the supreme recognition described here, the yogi apprehends the world as manifestation of their own universal conscious nature.

blocks.text: Not of their private personality.
blocks.directed: Not of their private personality.

blocks.text: Not of their ordinary ego.
blocks.directed: Not of their ordinary ego.

blocks.text: But of consciousness understood through the freedom of Śiva.
blocks.directed: But of consciousness understood through the freedom of Śiva.

blocks.text: And this is where the water-and-ice analogy becomes especially powerful.
blocks.directed: And this is where the water-and-ice analogy becomes especially powerful.

blocks.text: The ice doesn’t have to cease existing for its reality as water to be recognised.
blocks.directed: The ice doesn’t have to cease existing for its reality as water to be recognised.

blocks.text: Likewise, the world doesn’t have to physically disappear for its nondual nature to become apparent.
blocks.directed: Likewise, the world doesn’t have to physically disappear for its nondual nature to become apparent.

blocks.text: The form can remain.
blocks.directed: The form can remain.

blocks.text: The recognition changes.
blocks.directed: The recognition changes.

blocks.text: You were staring at the ice.
blocks.directed: You were staring at the ice.

blocks.text: Now you understand the water.
blocks.directed: Now you understand the water.

blocks.text: And suddenly Vasugupta makes an even more extraordinary declaration.
blocks.directed: And suddenly Vasugupta makes an even more extraordinary declaration.

blocks.text: Because if the yogi is established in this knowledge, apparently the entire cycle of rebirth comes to an end.
blocks.directed: Because if the yogi is established in this knowledge, apparently the entire cycle of rebirth comes to an end.

blocks.text: Now that’s quite an administrative achievement.
blocks.directed: Now that’s quite an administrative achievement.
